newsitem.title: UK: Ldn gold drops to 11-1/2 year low fix, looks lower.
newsitem.headline: Ldn gold drops to 11-1/2 year low fix, looks lower.

text.p: The gold price fixed at an 11-1/2 year low on Friday and dealers saw all the portents pointing to even lower prices next week.
The Reserve Bank of Australia announcement on Thursday that it had sold 167 tonnes of bullion from its reserves over the past six months sparked a delayed reaction in the markets.
Europe initally absorbed the information and took it as mildly positive.
But the speculative U.S. investment funds took a radically different view and read the signals as an invitation to sell.
As they did so, spot prices tumbled to around $323, marking a near 12-year low. In Asia, investors and dealers lined up to sell to be met by half-hearted physical offtake.
The result was that gold fixed at $325.25 per ounce in London, down from $332.55 on Thursday afternoon and a close of $331.30/$331.80.

"Things will probably stop this afternoon due to the American holiday," he said, referring to the closure of the New York market on Friday for the U.S. Independence Day holiday. "We are selling into areas which must be pretty near the low."
Even so there was plenty of selling to come, he added.
One source of distressed sales would be investors on the futures markets in Tokyo and New York curtting their losses by selling positions rather than meeting margin calls.
But there were also "many central banks wishing they had sold and gold producers wishing they had hedged," he said.
This could produce "an orgy of selling in the next few weeks to take it through $300," the dealer said.
After that there was a chance of a rally once the distressed selling had been cleared out.
Some dealers noted the aftermath of the Australian announcement was different from previous central bank sales.

"The forward market is telling me some people knew about this in advance," a dealer said, noting that there was no tightening of forward lending rates as there had been when the Dutch bank announced the sale of 300 tonnes in January.
Another dealer noted significant buying this week of short dated call options expiring today, and several pointed to the stepped up forward selling by Australian producers this week.
The other precious metals were also lower. Silver was at $5.54/$5.56, down 10 cents, platinum was down $5.00 at $418.00/$420.00 and palladium off $1.50 at $188.00/$192.00.
